title: First-Touch Provisioning: Snapshot Tiles, Autoscale Heuristics, and SLA Snapshot Flow
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description: Goal: Create a lightweight, scannable set of onboarding visuals that appear during a customer's first provisioning of Dedicated capacity. These assets should explain: (1) how the initial capacity snapshot is chosen, (2) autoscale heuristics that affect burst and steady-state behavior, and (3) an SLA snapshot that compares promised latency/uptime to the selected configuration. Scope: 6-8 UI tiles + 3 modal states + 4 microcopy tooltips + one full-width onboarding hero screenshot. Exclusions: deep dive documentation or training flows; those live in Confluence. Constraints: must fit into existing console grid (1024px container) and use the established design token palette and iconography. Deliver small, accessible components ready for dev handoff with Figma variants and an interaction prototype.
acceptance_criteria:
- Final Figma file with named components and 3 variants (Default, Low-Cost, High-Availability)
- Copy approved by Product and Growth
- Interactive prototype demonstrating: tile expand/collapse, autoscale slider preview, SLA comparison toggle
- Exported PNG/JPEG screenshots for release notes (desktop @2x)
- Handoff checklist completed and PR linked to console repo
design_links: Figma: Dedicated First Touch - Frame Set (file REQ-239)
visuals_overview:
1) Snapshot tiles (6): each tile summarizes a dimension (throughput, cost estimate, latency SLO, redundancy, burst capacity, region). Include numeric badges and microcopy.
2) Autoscale heuristics panel: visual timeline showing scale events, slider to preview target concurrency, and shorthand explanation of cooldown, buffer, and burst buckets.
3) SLA snapshot modal: side-by-side comparison of selected config vs recommended profile with risk indicators (green/yellow/red).
4) Failure & fallback states: when capacity cannot be reserved, show recommended fallbacks (reduce concurrency, select regional fallback, or switch to hosted) with CTAs.
5) Micro-interactions: subtle reveal of KV-cache benefit on hover, and transition animations for scale changes (200ms ease).
mock_variants: Low-cost - minimum reserved GPUs, aggressive autoscale (higher cold starts)
High-availability - more reserved capacity, multi-region fallback enabled

notes_for_engineering:
- Use telemetry keys as provided by ENG-55123; tiles should poll at 5s intervals but expose a static preview image for first-run to avoid spinners.
- Autoscale slider is a design-only preview; actual change must call the autoscale API. Provide a 'Preview only' label.
- All numeric values should have a fallback '—' state.
- Include data hooks: data-test-id attributes for each tile: tile-throughput, tile-cost, tile-latency, tile-redundancy, tile-burst, tile-region.
- See PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1427 for starting components.

accessibility_considerations:
- All interactive tiles must be keyboard-focusable with visible focus rings.
- Color alone must not convey risk; use icons + text (e.g., green check, amber warning, red alert).
- Provide aria-live regions for SLA snapshot updates so screen reader users get notified when numbers change.
localization_requirements: Short strings only in tiles (<= 40 chars) and tooltip copy separate for translation. Reserve room for 30% expansion in UI. Coordinate with L10n to extract copy keys before 2026-03-12.
